citations.review_text:
The OG Slavik Cynical Greed Scam that ruined Military Vehicle Combat Games for decades now.
Whats to say, it fullfilles (if not made) all the stereotypical Post Soviet Union State Jank and Free-To-Play Bait And Switch Manipulation you can think of. And probably has already created some new ones you haven´t heard about, yet.
The gameplay is as basic ♥♥♥♥♥ as it can get. Of Course Primarily PvP, because they really want to force you into buying there Pay-To-Win. With everything being poorly balanced, executed, general designed,  either to frustrate you into buying better gear to alleviate the suffering by becoming the OP Pay-To-Win Bully or make room on the server by makeing you quite after 2-3 games. Cause your precious daily login is all what they need to sell the play numbers to potential investors.

Don´t expect an sympathy, passion or generally something good from the people behind this company, they have non and likely never had any to begin with. Its all just for the money, like every Free-To-Play game.

Have i told you yet about the pricing? The pricing of ANYTHING in this "Pretends to be" game? Oh boy, if you ain´t atleast a Millionare, you won´t be happy with this.

Though the worst is, there is no syncing with the OG World of Tanks, yet this game has some content that the OG doesn´t have and vice versa. So if you want to have something from Blitz and something from the OG World of Tanks have fun grinding and paying through the same content TWICE.
A pretty worse tank that need heavy pay to win and grinding.

Played the game in past on phone  and decided to try it again. Sadly it went way down hill and keeps getting more greedy. Events they want you to grind double the amount to get the end rewards. They increased prices, changed drop rates etc.  Also matching is not that good, to many afks in this game.

I’ve dipped in and out of World of Tanks Blitz for a good while now, and honestly, it’s a solid little tank battler… provided you accept it for what it is: a mobile game that’s somehow ended up living on PC

The matches are fast, easy to jump into, and surprisingly tactical when you actually get a team that isn’t trying to reenact a lemming migration. The tank models look tidy, the controls are smooth, and there’s a decent sense of progression early on.

But let’s not kid ourselves — the monetisation creeps in quickly. Premium tanks, premium time, crates, events that feel like they’re run by someone who’s got a quota to meet… you get the idea. You can play completely free, but you’ll feel the grind tightening the further you go. And balance? Sometimes spot-on, sometimes “how is that thing legal?”

Still, it is fun. Quick matches, good mechanics, and enough variety to keep you entertained if you’re after something more casual than the full-fat PC version.

My Opine 7/10 — enjoyable and accessible, but weighed down by mobile-game monetisation.

citations.review_text: The way this game runs is quite frankly inexcusable.  I don't exactly have the most powerful rig in the world... I mean, this computer I'm on is ancient.  But even I should be able to run this game decently.  Even on the lowest settings, there are massive stutters and frame skips that just make it too much of a headache.  I really would like to play it a bit more, but I just can't justify putting any more time into it than I have.

Please prioritize CPU optimization and proper multi core utilization in World of Tanks: HEAT.

Modern processors commonly have 12, 16, 24, 32 and 48 CPU cores, yet many games still overload only a few main threads while leaving much of the CPU underused. This can cause CPU bottlenecks, frame time spikes, stuttering, weak 1% lows, and reduced performance during large battles.

Vehicle simulation, physics, destruction, animation, audio, asset streaming, networking, visibility calculations, and rendering preparation should be distributed more efficiently across available CPU cores. The goal should not only be higher average FPS, but also smoother frame pacing, better responsiveness, and stable performance during the most demanding battles.

The developers should also take advantage of modern AI-assisted development tools to accelerate engine optimization. AI can help analyze profiling data, identify expensive code paths, detect synchronization problems, generate performance tests, review threading code, and find regressions faster. However, the final implementation must still be carefully designed, tested, and validated by experienced engine programmers.

Please build the engine to scale properly across modern CPUs instead of relying too heavily on one or two main threads. Strong multi threading, efficient task scheduling, and AI assisted profiling could significantly improve performance and help the game remain technically competitive for years.

citations.review_text: World of Tanks Blitz is an awesome and enduring tactical PvP shooter that scales down the classic tank warfare experience into punchy, adrenaline-fueled matches. What I really love about it is the sheer variety of vehicles—spanning over 600 machines from historical powerhouses to wild experimental blueprints—alongside tight map design and responsive gunplay. The cross-platform matchmaking makes jumping into a match with friends effortless, and the constant stream of events keeps the meta fresh. While the grind can feel heavy and premium content can get pricey, the core loop of angling your armor, outsmarting opponents, and landing that perfect shell is endlessly rewarding. Highly recommend it if you enjoy strategic vehicle combat on the go!

World of Tanks Blitz is a free-to-play online multiplayer tank combat game developed and published by Wargaming Group Limited. Built around fast-paced armored warfare, it delivers an experience that emphasizes accessibility without sacrificing tactical depth. Rather than focusing on prolonged battles, the game keeps matches short and intense, allowing players to jump into seven-versus-seven engagements that reward quick thinking, teamwork, and strategic positioning. This design makes it easy to enjoy a few battles in a short session while still offering enough complexity to keep dedicated players invested over the long term.

A major highlight is its enormous collection of armored vehicles. Players can command hundreds of tanks inspired by real military history alongside prototype designs and experimental machines. Every vehicle feels unique thanks to differences in armor, speed, firepower, gun handling, and battlefield role. Light tanks excel at scouting and mobility, medium tanks offer versatility, heavy tanks dominate the front lines with thick armor, and tank destroyers specialize in devastating long-range attacks. Progressing through the various technology trees is satisfying because every newly unlocked vehicle introduces a different tactical experience rather than serving as a simple numerical upgrade.

The combat system successfully blends arcade-style action with meaningful strategy. Controls are responsive and approachable for newcomers, but experienced players quickly discover the importance of understanding terrain, hull positioning, armor angling, concealment, ammunition selection, and coordinated team play. Charging into battle without a plan often leads to quick destruction, while patient and calculated decisions can completely shift the outcome of a match. The game's relatively short battles create constant tension, encouraging players to stay engaged from beginning to end while rewarding both mechanical skill and sound tactical judgment.

I have over 6000 battles in this game and at the time of writing this nearly 1300 hours. Now, I will preface this by saying that I am not a fully F2P player. I have bought multiple things from the in-game store. HOWEVER. This game is not P2W. You can actually get a bunch of free stuff by just playing the game and opening whatever free crates you get. There's almost always an in-game event going on that gives you free stuff. Yes, a lot of the tanks you have to buy with real money are good (some would say OP). However you still have to know how to play them properly and how the game mechanics work in order to do well in them. Otherwise you will most likely get called all sorts of things by your teammates for how dumb and stupid you are. This game is a lot faster paced than WOTPC so if you're expecting the slower battles of PC, I'm sorry but that's not this. Battles last up to 7 minutes but are on average around 3 - 5 mins. There can actually be quite a lot of strategy involved, but there are also fun gamemodes that don't affect your WR at all (if you're concerned about that) that can be quite a lot of fun. This game is not for everyone but personally I would recommend giving it a shot.

Edit: Note that this was made prior to the Reforged Update's release. I will most likely edit this review once it releases if anything has changed.
